_comment: Machine-readable companion to scenario-catalog.md, ordered per skill-ladder.md. Consumed by scripts/orderflow_drill.py [st-5ov]. Bar indices are valid ONLY at bar_n below; the drill falls back to level-arming when bar sizes differ. Never guess a reference — [to tag] scenarios ship with refs: []. Revised 2026-09-10 (st-z1a1): direction is an axis — every S ref carries side (down = at a support, the bullish read; up = at a resistance, the bearish read) and kind; labels lead with the arrow. Upside refs pinned from replay records 20260910T170437943328Z-f60a18d (07-02), 20260910T170553697346Z-f60a18d (07-20), 20260910T170905249481Z-f60a18d (08-19) under the kind rule (st-tme). Never pool the sides in a measurement without the per-side split. Known drift in the 07-02 down refs: st-r88d.

scenarios.name: Tempo — pace reading
scenarios.what: T1 heating (durations shortening), T2 dead tape (long bars, dim columns), T3 burst (seconds-long bars — an event on the tape). The pace strip is the instrument; the skill is feeling it before looking at it.
scenarios.tell: Time is an output, not an input: same contracts per bar, wildly different clock. T3 bursts are often stage 1 of an S2 somewhere.
scenarios.call: No call — this unit calibrates urgency perception.

T3 burst — six bars in 31 seconds at 14:59, the final 7483 defense

scenarios.name: Frames — single-cell reading
scenarios.what: The effort-vs-effect matrix: F1 conviction (bright, big number), F2 absorption (bright, small number — reversal fuel), F3 hollow (dim, big number), F4 dead. Effort = brightness, score = the net number.
scenarios.tell: F2 is the money quadrant: huge strain, arm didn't move — someone strong is hiding.
scenarios.call: No call — these are the stage detectors for everything above them.

refs.label: F2 absorption — bar 0: a net −1 cell brighter than the −16 cell (Steve's first-bar find)

scenarios.name: Failed break (the trap) — ↓ failed breakdown / ↑ failed breakout
scenarios.what: Aggressors break the level with real force, the break stops paying, the other side takes over, price retakes the level. The full four-stage sequence with a violent flush. ↓ Failed breakdown at a support (failed_breakdown, bullish — Mancini's signature setup). ↑ Failed breakout at a resistance (failed_breakout, bearish — the bull trap): blue through the lid, stall with no new highs, footers turn red, close back beneath.
scenarios.tell: vs S4 (clean break): stage 2 is the tell — in S2 the aggressors stop getting paid beyond the level; in S4 the break keeps producing new extremes at pace.
scenarios.call: After confirm: go with the retake — bullish at a support, bearish at a resistance. Before confirm: hands off.

scenarios.name: Clean break (the anti-trap) — ↓ breakdown holds / ↑ breakout holds
scenarios.what: The level breaks and STAYS broken: force with effect, no stall, no flip. What looks like the start of S2 but the trap never springs. ↓ the floor gives way and the lows keep coming (invalidated: no reclaim). ↑ the lid gives way and the highs keep coming (invalidated: held above, no reject).
scenarios.tell: Does the aggression keep getting paid? Paid → continuation; unpaid → trap forming. Never fade force that is being paid.

scenarios.name: Sprung trap fails (stall without retake)
scenarios.what: The pattern gets to stage 2 or 3 — the aggressors stall, delta even flips — but the retake never comes; price grinds back through the would-be retake level. ↓ blue pressure fails at the level from below, footers revert red. ↑ red pressure fails at the level from above, footers revert blue. Lifecycle ends invalidated.
scenarios.tell: Only the confirm stage separates this from S2/S3 in progress — which is exactly why the call waits for stage 4. This scenario is why.
scenarios.call: No trade. If positioned early (against doctrine), the fast cut.

scenarios.name: Quiet retake (the gentle sibling) — ↓ level reclaim / ↑ level reject
scenarios.what: Same destination as S2 — price back on the right side of a lost level with opposite evidence — but the flush lacked violence; the level was lost quietly rather than trapped. ↓ Level reclaim at a support (level_reclaim, bullish). ↑ Level reject at a resistance (level_reject, bearish — a quiet poke above the lid, retaken from above; the recognizer's only 'reject', and not S1: here the level trades through first).
scenarios.tell: vs S2: how the level was LOST — violently (S2) or quietly (S3). Mancini himself relabels between these siblings; family-level agreement is success.
scenarios.call: Go with the retake on confirm; slightly lower conviction than a true trap.

scenarios.name: Clean hold (was: clean rejection)
scenarios.what: Price approaches the level, aggression into it is punished immediately, price leaves the way it came. The level holds on first contact — it never trades through. ↓ at a support: sellers punished, price leaves upward (bullish reaction). ↑ at a resistance: buyers punished, price leaves downward (bearish reaction).
scenarios.tell: vs S2: in S1 the level never trades through; S2's flush begins the same way an approach does.
scenarios.call: Held — fade the approach (price bounces ≥4 points away). The button still reads Reject until st-g9y reconciles the judgment verbs.

scenarios.name: Chop straddle
scenarios.what: Price oscillates across the level with conviction in neither direction. The level is noise today, or the tape is resting on it. Direction-neutral by construction — there is no ↓/↑ instance, which is the story's content.
scenarios.tell: vs S1: S1 leaves the level after holding; S6 keeps coming back with no force either way.
scenarios.call: No call. Neither 4-point move within 10 bars = chop, no credit for guessing.

scenarios.name: Anchor generalization (Carmine's set)
scenarios.what: The same ladder re-met at other anchor types: the sequence at a support level = failed_breakdown / level_reclaim, at a range edge = range_trap, at an LVN = return_to_lvn. Carmine's four strats are (one sequence) × (three anchor types), not four curricula.
scenarios.tell: The Anatomy list on this page already labels each recognized setup by its anchor kind — walk range_trap and return_to_lvn instances there.
scenarios.call: Per the underlying scenario (S1–S6) — the anchor changes where, not what.
